html:<strong>Andelsbolig</strong>: <stro: Housing co-op flat (andelsbolig): The price is set by the association's general meeting (maximum price) — it cannot legally exceed this value. This means a cap on appreciation. The buyer must be approved by the board. The time to sell is often longer, and you can't reject applicants based on price.
html:<strong>Andelsbolig</strong>: Bankl: Housing co-op flat (andelsbolig): Bank loans, not mortgages (realkredit). Shorter terms (typically ⟦0⟧–⟦1⟧ years), higher interest rates (⟦2⟧–⟦3⟧ %), lower LTV (some banks cap at ⟦4⟧–⟦5⟧ %). The monthly payment per krone borrowed is significantly higher.
html:<strong>Andelsbolig</strong>: Du ej: Housing co-op flat (andelsbolig): You own a share in the association that owns the building. You have the right of use to a specific flat, not ownership. The rules for letting, selling and pricing are governed by the association's articles of association.
html:<strong>Andelsbolig</strong>: Hvis: Housing co-op flat (andelsbolig): If letting is allowed: same tax logic applies. But the sale gain is often capped by the maximum price, so there's rarely much capital gain to tax.
html:<strong>Andelsbolig</strong>: Måned: Housing co-op flat (andelsbolig): Monthly "housing fee" typically DKK ⟦0⟧–⟦1⟧. It covers the association's shared loan plus operating costs. Higher because it includes a form of housing debt you share with your neighbours.
html:<strong>Andelsbolig</strong>: Vedtæ: Housing co-op flat (andelsbolig): The articles of association decide. Many associations only allow subletting for up to ⟦0⟧ years with documented temporary absence (work abroad, illness). Some ban letting entirely. A handful of liberal associations allow it, but they're rare.
html:<strong>BRRRR i en liberal forening: BRRRR in a liberal association — if you find one of the rare associations that allows letting with no time limit, and the price is well below market level, it could be a deal.
html:<strong>Egen bolig med henblik på s: Own home with a view to subletting later — some associations allow ⟦0⟧ years of subletting. If you're planning a gap year abroad, you can live there first and let it out later.
html:<strong>Ejerlejlighed</strong>: Du: Owner-occupied flat (condo): You own the flat itself directly. It's registered in your name at the land registry, you hold a deed, and you can sell, mortgage and let it on market terms (within the bounds of the law).
html:<strong>Ejerlejlighed</strong>: Fri: Owner-occupied flat (condo): Unrestricted right to let, only limited by the Rent Control Act (which applies to all landlords). You can let it out immediately and on an open-ended contract.
html:<strong>Ejerlejlighed</strong>: Lej: Owner-occupied flat (condo): Rental income is taxed under a scheme of your choice (personal, the business tax scheme (virksomhedsordningen), or a private limited company). Interest and operating costs are tax-deductible. On sale, the gain is taxed (unless it's your primary residence for at least a year).
html:<strong>Ejerlejlighed</strong>: Mån: Owner-occupied flat (condo): Monthly contribution to the owners' association typically DKK ⟦0⟧–⟦1⟧ covers shared operating costs.
html:<strong>Ejerlejlighed</strong>: Pri: Owner-occupied flat (condo): The market sets the price. Free sale, active estate agents, average time to sell ⟦0⟧–⟦1⟧ days in the major cities.
html:<strong>Ejerlejlighed</strong>: Rea: Owner-occupied flat (condo): Mortgages (realkredit) up to ⟦0⟧ % LTV, ⟦1⟧-year terms, fixed or variable rates. In ⟦2⟧, typical rates are ⟦3⟧–⟦4⟧ % depending on loan type and LTV.
html:<strong>For investorer</strong>: Hv: For investors: If the right to let is limited to ⟦0⟧ years, you can't build a cash flow portfolio. Full stop. Read the articles of association before you even consider making an offer.

html:Til <strong>investering</strong> er: For investment, an owner-occupied flat is almost always the right choice. Housing co-op flats are cheaper to buy into, but most housing co-op associations ban or strictly restrict letting, and financing is more expensive and less flexible. A housing co-op flat can make sense as a home — as an investment it's usually not suitable.
For everything else: buy an owner-occupied flat (condo).
